newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders mixed.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent per lb lower while calls ranged from 0.150 cent lower to 0.100 higher for feeder cattle futures, livestock analysts said.

Weakness in fed cattle and boxed beef markets were expected to keep pressure on nearby live cattle futures. Packers lowered their bids for fed cattle down to $63 per cwt after cattle traded down to $64 Tuesday, the lowest price level since February, analysts said.
However, distant months may hold steady as feedlot placements are seen tapering off after June, they said.
Most analysts look for carryover technical pressure in feeder cattle futures. The market turned technically weak on Tuesday's break and some analysts also look for the CME index to turn lower soon.
However, others noted the index continued to advance and with lower indications on corn futures could provide underlying support to the market.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.32 to $77.74 per cwt, they highest level since August 19, 1994.
